config.title: SovNode (Aider-style)
config.model.description: Model to use. The PROVIDER is detected from the name: gemini-* uses Gemini, gpt-*/o<number>-* uses OpenAI, claude-* uses Anthropic. Each provider needs its own API key (🔑 button or "SovNode: Set API Key"). "auto" = Auto mode: SovNode picks the model for each turn by rules (see sovnodeAider.autoModels and /auto).
config.effort.description: Reasoning budget and output token ceiling.
config.streaming.description: Show the response and thoughts live (streaming). If it fails due to the network, it retries automatically in normal mode.
config.autoCommit.description: If the folder is a git repo, make a commit for each applied change (only with the files SovNode touched).
config.architect.description: Architect mode (like Aider): the main model first writes a plan (no code) and then the editor model implements it with SEARCH/REPLACE blocks. Better for large or multi-file changes; costs one extra call.
config.editorModel.description: Model that writes the code in architect mode (e.g. gemini-3.1-flash-lite to save money). It can be from a DIFFERENT provider than the main one (e.g. gemini-3.6-flash plans, gpt-6-luna edits) -- each uses its own API key. Empty = the same main model.
config.editFormat.description: Format in which the model writes changes (as in Aider). Also via /format in the chat.
config.editFormat.enumDescriptions.auto: Choose automatically based on the model writing the code: small ones (lite/luna/haiku/mini) -> whole file; OpenAI -> unified diff; the rest -> SEARCH/REPLACE.
config.editFormat.enumDescriptions.searc: SEARCH/REPLACE blocks (the usual format). Cheap in tokens; requires copying the exact text.
config.editFormat.enumDescriptions.udiff: Unified diff (like git diff). Tolerant: if a hunk does not match whole, it is tried split and with the line number from the @@.
config.editFormat.enumDescriptions.whole: Rewrite the whole file. The most reliable for small models, but expensive on large files.
config.maxAutoSteps.description: Maximum number of steps an autonomous task (/task) is split into. A model splits the request and then each step runs on its own, one after another.
config.verify.description: After applying a change, check that the touched file(s) compile/parse (Python, JavaScript, JSON for now) and, if it fails, let the model fix itself before committing.
config.verifyCommand.description: Optional command to run in addition to the syntax check (e.g. "npm test", "pytest -q"). Runs in the project folder; if it fails, it also triggers self-correction.
config.verifyTimeoutMs.description: Maximum time for sovnodeAider.verifyCommand before considering it hung.
config.includeActiveFile.description: Automatically include the editor's active file in the context.
config.openChangedFiles.description: Open the first changed/created file at the line of the change.
config.maxHistoryTurns.description: How many previous conversation turns are resent to the model (with slack: it is pruned in batches, not turn by turn, to avoid breaking the provider cache -- it may go a few turns over before pruning).
config.chatFileIdleTurns.description: Files SovNode added to the chat on its own (the ones it created, or that the model asked for) are removed from the chat after this many turns without being edited, named in a request or log, or open in the editor. They stay in the repo map and the model can ask for them again. Files you add yourself (/add) are never removed. Every file in the chat is resent in full on every call, so this saves tokens in long sessions. 0 = disabled.
config.focusLargeFiles.description: Focused context: for files with at least this many lines, only the parts the request touches (named functions, lines from a log, the selection) plus an index of the rest are sent, instead of the whole file. If the request names nothing specific, the whole file is sent. The model can ask for the full file. 0 = disabled.
config.repoMapCache.description: Sends the repository map as a separate stable block at the start of the request (identical turn to turn, so the provider bills it as cache) instead of mixed in with the files and the question. What depends on the request (the symbols you name, with their current line) goes separately and small.
config.architectBaseCache.description: Architect mode: the architect receives each file once as a 'base version' at the start of the request (identical turn to turn, so the provider bills it as cache) and then only the diff of what changed. If the changes exceed a third of the file, the base is renewed. The editor still receives the current code.
config.toolsMaxRounds.description: Micro-tools: how many rounds per turn the model can request 'read' or 'search' before answering. Empty (null) = based on Effort: low 1, medium 2, high 3, extra 5. A number sets it for all. 0 = disabled. What the model already has is not resent.
config.execEnabled.description: Allows the model to request RUNNING a command mid-turn (build, run a specific test) in addition to read/search. You are always asked to confirm each command (unless you choose 'trust' or the command is in sovnodeAider.execAllowlist). Ignored if sovnodeAider.toolsMaxRounds is 0.
config.execTimeoutMs.description: Maximum time (ms) a command requested by the model may run before it is stopped. Hard limit: 120000 (2 minutes).
config.execAllowlist.description: Commands (or the exact start of a command, e.g. 'npm test') that run WITHOUT asking for confirmation each time. Leave empty to always be asked. An always-blocked command (mass deletion, formatting, etc.) is never bypassed by this.
config.sessionLogKeep.description: How many session log files (one per time this VS Code window is opened, with full detail of each turn) are kept; older ones are deleted automatically. 0 = keep none (only usage.jsonl, the usual summary, remains).
config.extendedThinking.description: Anthropic only: enables 'extended thinking' (the model thinks before answering) when the turn's Effort is 'high' or 'extra'. On low/medium it stays off. Gemini and OpenAI already think according to Effort without this setting.
config.pricing.description: Overrides USD prices per million tokens, e.g.: {"gemini-3.6-flash": {"input": 0.75, "output": 3.75}}
config.projectMemory.description: Sends .sovnode/memoria.md (your notes about the project: conventions, decisions, 'do not touch') at the start of each request, as a cacheable block. If the file does not exist or is empty it costs nothing. Create/open it with 'SovNode: Edit project memory'.
config.agentMode.description: Agent mode for /task: if a step fails (error, edits that do not apply, or verification that gives up), it retries with the real error (up to 2 times) and if it gets stuck on the same error it replans what remains (once). Off: /task stops at the first failure. Costs more when something fails. Also /agent or the 🤖 button.
config.taskBudgetUSD.description: Agent mode: budget in USD per task (/task). When reached, it pauses and asks whether to continue (another equal amount) or stop. 0 = no limit.
config.nativeTools.description: The model's tools (read, search, files, run) are sent as NATIVE API calls (Gemini/OpenAI/Anthropic) instead of the 'HERRAMIENTAS:' text protocol. Large models use them better (fewer wasted rounds). If a model rejects them, it falls back to the text protocol for the rest of the session. Off = always text.
config.agentStepModel.description: Agent mode: CHEAP model that performs the /task steps (e.g. gemini-3.6-flash). The main model plans and, if a step fails, the retry escalates to the main model for that step only. Empty = steps use the main model. Also /stepmodel <model>.
config.autoModels.description: Auto mode (model = "auto" or /auto): sets which model each tier is. Empty = chosen automatically among the models with an API key, by output price (the cheapest, the middle and the most expensive). E.g.: {"barato": "gemini-3.6-flash", "medio": "claude-sonnet-5", "fuerte": "claude-opus-5-5"}.
config.language.description: Interface language. auto = follow VS Code's display language (Spanish if VS Code is in Spanish, otherwise English).
config.autoEscalate.description: Auto mode: if a turn done by a non-strong model fails verifiably (changes couldn't be applied, or verification failed), revert it and retry once with the strong model. API/network errors don't escalate.
